segments.text: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, once described his own followers' future... and it was not flattering. He said they would copy the nations before them... so exactly... that no hole would be too small to crawl into.
segments._shot: cracked desert earth, a dark burrow entrance

segments.text: This is the warning... of the lizard's hole.
segments.title: SPAN BY SPAN
segments.titleSub: a warning to his own people
segments._shot: slow sand drifting across dark stone

segments.text: First, the setting. The Qur'an and the Prophet, peace be upon him, speak often of the nations before Islam... communities given guidance, who then drifted, divided, and traded their religion piece by piece for fashion and power. The warning was that his own people were not immune.
segments._shot: ruins of an ancient city, wind-blown

segments.text: You will follow the ways of those nations who were before you... he said... span by span, and cubit by cubit... inch by inch... so much so that even if they entered a hole of a lizard, you would follow them.

The companions asked... do you mean the Jews and the Christians? He said... whom else? Not spoken in contempt... the earlier nations are the only map of how a believing people slowly becomes something else.
segments._shot: a worn path splitting off a straight road

segments.text: Notice the unit of measure. Not leaps. Spans. A hand-width at a time. No one abandons what they believe in a day... they inch away from it, each step too small to feel like a decision.
segments._shot: macro of sand grains slipping over an edge

segments.text: Fourteen centuries later, the prophecy reads like a mirror... imitation, inch by inch, all the way down into the smallest holes of culture. The warning was recorded so you could catch yourself mid-span. Which direction are your inches going?
segments._shot: dawn light over a long, straight desert road
